page: Microsoft Azure E64a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EAv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7452 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 1638 GB SSD, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate a clear contrast between single-core and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core and parallel execution metrics are robust; the Passmark CPU score and Passmark CPU encryption test both rank in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs strongly in the top 25%. Memory performance is solid, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top 25%, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 106.39 GB/sec. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with text generation on a medium 7B model scoring in the bottom 10%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and bundled 1.6 TB local SSD, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound applications without requiring external storage attachments for scratch space. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for workloads that demand substantial memory footprints but do not require top-tier single-core CPU speeds. The E64a_v4 is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems, multi-threaded data decompression, and enterprise application hosting.
description: The Microsoft Azure E64a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores. Operating at 3.525 GHz, this x86_64 server is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes a 1638 GB local SSD. While single-core benchmarks like stress-ng place in the bottom 10%, its multi-threaded capabilities are robust, with Passmark CPU and memory scores ranking in the top 25%. The server delivers strong multi-threaded decompression and encryption performance, though it exhibits weak results in large-model LLM inference. This configuration is highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, including large databases, in-memory analytics, and enterprise applications requiring substantial local storage.
